title: Strength-weighted primary adoption criterion for the afterstate tournaments (arms A, B, C, three-way and multi-arm)
registered_before: any tournament, three-way or multi-arm adoption game is played
decided_by: the user, relayed by the main session
applies_to: arm B and the three-way tournament (trainer/afterstate-core-human)
arm C and the multi-arm tournament (trainer/afterstate-core-full)

primary.statistic: strength-weighted pooled score: sum_p w_p * score_p with the normalized weights; its 95% interval from the same whole-seed bootstrap resamples as the per-pace scores
primary.PROMOTE: weighted pooled 95% lower bound > 0.50 AND no pace with simultaneous 95% upper bound < 0.45
primary.PARITY: not PROMOTE AND weighted pooled 95% interval contains 0.50 AND no pace with simultaneous 95% upper bound < 0.45

secondary: the equal-weight pooled score and its interval (the previously registered primary) are reported alongside, with its PROMOTE/PARITY/REJECT verdict, but no longer decide adoption
justification: absolute strength matters most at the fast paces; the slow paces use human-like movement in the product and weaker players choose slower paces
unchanged: arm A stop rule: equal-weight pooled panel score, two consecutive non-improving snapshots. It already evaluated three snapshots (distill-v1 0.525, 50M 0.568, 100M 0.595); changing it now would be post hoc, so it stays exactly as registered. Arms B and C keep their registered stop rules likewise.
seeds, schedules, per-pace simultaneous bands, the shipped-timing confirmation (pooled lower bound >= 0.45) and the three-way/multi-arm finals structure
